subject: Inference scan: latency & throughput goals, topology options
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sam Wong <sam.wong@atlascare.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jul 2029 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Inference scan: latency & throughput goals, topology options

Hi Sam — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick written recap so everyone has the same picture and we can prioritize the technical deep dive: 

Summary of what you shared
- Primary product: AtlasCare triage assistant (real-time suggestions during provider intake).
- Current pain: unpredictable tail latency during morning spikes; 95th/99th spikes frequently exceed target windows and cause UI timeouts for clinicians.
- Current throughput target for inference: sustained 120–150 reqs/s with 1–3s average end-to-end budget at the application layer.
- Desired SLOs: p95 < 100ms server-side generation; p99 < 200ms; cold-start / model-switch fallback within 500ms.
- Model constraints: using a trimmed Llama-based model (~7B) with max input tokens ~1024; minimal additional pre/post-processing CPU overhead.
- Compliance note: PHI is present in some requests; AtlasCare prefers private VPC option for production.

What Redwood suggested on the call (high level)
- Run a mixed topology: dedicated pools for steady-state traffic + hosted autoscale for safe burst capacity; model-variant routing for graceful degradation.
- Aggressive KV prefix caching for repeat prompts (expected 20–35% token savings).
- Quantized 4-bit model variant for cost-sensitive fallbacks; full-precision for primary SLO lane.

Asks / next steps (proposed)
1) We’ll prepare an initial latency-budget back-of-envelope and a topology sketch (attached: topology-sketch-v1.png, latency-budget-calc.xlsx).
2) Karthik to propose a deployment mapping (dedicated pool sizes, GPU types, burst policy) and expected p95/p99 numbers based on your request distribution.
3) Schedule a dedicated technical deep-dive (60m) with your infra/DevOps + our runtime team next week to validate assumptions and test a short synthetic load.

Sam — can you confirm: 1) whether the 120–150 reqs/s estimate is peak or sustained during a 15m window, and 2) whether the PHI requests require air-gapped on-prem deploys or a VPC endpoint is sufficient?

Thanks — attaching the call notes and topology sketch for reference.

Best,

Thanks Olga — appreciate the clear recap. Confirmations below: 

- The 120–150 reqs/s is our expected sustained peak across the daytime triage window (roughly 09:00–15:00 PT) for the initial region; we could see bursts up to ~250 reqs/s for brief periods when multiple intake streams align.
- PHI handling: VPC with customer-managed KMS is our preference for production. Air-gapped on-prem would be a later possibility for some high-compliance sites, but not required at initial launch.

Couple of follow-ups: 
- Can you provide an estimate for tokens per request (we hit ~350 tokens average today after pre/post processing)? That will affect GPU memory/caching sizing.
- We’re curious about the tradeoffs you mentioned for the 4-bit quantized fallback vs full precision for p99 behavior — does quantization risk large p99 regressions?

Happy to join the technical deep-dive — our infra lead, Priya Natarajan, will join as well (cc’d in a separate thread). Can we do 2029-07-18 10:00 PT?

Subject: Re: Inference scan: latency & throughput goals, topology options

Sam — quick technical note ahead of the deep-dive; I ran a first-pass sizing using the numbers you provided and a conservative token estimate of 350 tokens/request. Key points: 

1) Token budget & GPU memory
- 350 tokens average with Llama-7B-like architecture (KV cache for the prompt + 1024 max) maps cleanly to a 24GB GPU for the pop/p99 lane when using 4-bit quantization (8-bit or fp16 for primary). If you insist on fp16-only primary, consider A100-40GB or partitioned approach.

2) Throughput and batching assumptions
- Sustained 150 reqs/s: with dynamic batching and 4-bit kernels we estimate ~120–180 tokens/s per GPU depending on sequence-length variance. That implies a baseline pool of 2–4 x A10s (or 1–2 x A100-40) for steady-state with an additional burst pool sized to absorb 250 reqs/s peaks.

3) Latency SLOs (p95/p99) — conservative expectation
- Primary lane (fp16, moderate batching, active KV cache): p95 ~ 60–90ms; p99 ~ 160–240ms depending on batch windows and request coalescing.
- Fallback lane (4-bit quantized variant): p95 ~ 40–70ms (smaller execution time), but p99 can widen if load imbalance causes queueing — this is an operational effect, not solely a quantization artifact.

4) Operational mitigations for p99 spikes
- Per-request routing policy: short-circuit heavy requests to a hot standby (dedicated small pool) if queue depth > threshold.
- Prefix/KV cache warmers during known busy windows to reduce cold-starts.
- Autoscale headroom with pre-warmed burst VMs (dedicated capacity + host autoscale).

5) Compliance/topology options (mapping to Redwood product lines)
- VPC control plane (preferred): Keeps control plane hosted but data plane in your VPC; integrates with your KMS — lowest friction and supports PHI.
- Private on-prem agent: full air-gapped option (longer lead time).
- Hybrid (recommended): initial rollout on VPC + reserved Dedicated pools for the steady lane; fallbacks routed to hosted (non-PHI) or quantized lane where appropriate.

Attachments: I attached a first-pass latency-budget calculation and a simple sketch of a mixed topology. These are intentionally conservative so we can tighten after we see real telemetry.

Question for you both: can you export a small representative traffic trace (anonymized) or a histogram of request sizes/arrivals? That will let me replace assumptions with measured values and update pool sizing.

Karthik

Perfect — thanks Sam, Karthik. 2029-07-18 10:00 PT works for us; I’ll send a calendar invite with an agenda: 1) validate request histogram (15m), 2) review topology options and sizing (25m), 3) run-through failover/routing policies and next steps (15m), 4) confirm pilot success criteria and timeline (5m).

Action items for the meeting: 
- AtlasCare: share anonymized traffic histogram or five-minute trace + confirmation that VPC+KMS flow is acceptable.
- Redwood: finalize a candidate Dedicated pool sizing matrix + suggested GPU SKUs, and bring a short demo of KV cache warmers.

I attached the call notes again and the sketches so attendees can review beforehand. If Priya (infra lead) wants to share any operational constraints ahead of time please include them in the thread.

Thanks — see you tomorrow.
Olga
